main_text.p: let enim factum aliquod reprehendi: quia turpe & inhonestum: quia cū damno vel publico, vel priuato coniunctum: quia difficile, ac periculosum: quia rarū, inusitatū, à nullo ante, aut paucis, iisque improbis sufceptum. Vtile autem in eiuscemodi sactorum vituperatione Aristotelis est præceptum, qui monet, vt factis vitiorum nomina imponamus, & μεταχρηματισμῷ transfiguratione quadá vtamur. Tractatio atq; collocatio ita instituenda: vt in exordio cum dolore quodam atque indignatione scriptionis susceptæ causæ indicetur: parte altera factum ipsum reprehēdatur atq; exaggeretur: tertia occurratur iis quæ pur gandi causa adferri posse videntur: postre ma, adhortatio, aut territatio adhibeatur. Exemplum tale esse poterit.
I. Etsi perinuitus faciam, te vt reprehendam: & si quisquam alius à vituperationibus abhorreat: tamen amicitiæ nostræ fides ac religio requirit: vt vituperare hoc te tempore minimè verear.
II. Quid enim per Deum immortalem agis, aut quid tandem cogitas?
III. Nemo à vobis ad nos venit (veniunt aut plurimi) quin de tua auaritia ac tyrannide conqueratur: idem multorum bonorum ad nos perscriptæ literæ confirmant.

page.notes: Doubtful or not checked: the page is photographed at an angle and the left edge of the text is shadowed; words at the line ends may be cut off. Greek word in the paragraph beginning "let enim" (μεταχαρακτηρισμῷ-type term) is read as printed as far as the scan allows: "μεταχρηματισμῷ" is uncertain and marked here as [?] in spirit, not in the text. Printed "sactorum" in the sentence "Vtile autem in eiuscemodi factorum" is copied as printed; the scan shows "fa" followed by a catchword-like break, so the reading may be "factorum" with a line-end hyphen missing. Ornamental "trans-figuratione" is set with a hyphen at line end and joined here.
